patches.old_text: Stripe automatically sorts buttons by relevance to the customer's location. When the element has determined which wallets are available, it fires a `ready` event with `availablePaymentMethods`.
patches.new_text: Stripe sorts eligible buttons by relevance to the customer's location. The November 2026 overview uses `availablepaymentmethodschange` with `paymentMethods` to check availability in the customer's current environment; its React prop is `onAvailablePaymentMethodsChange`. The April 2026 overview used `ready` with `availablePaymentMethods` for this check. The captures do not establish removal of `ready` for every purpose or actual payment completion.
patches.reason: Replace the unqualified older availability callback with dated April/November event scopes.

patches.old_text: Firefox does not support Apple Pay, Link, or Klarna. All payment methods have limited or no support in in-app webviews — use the iOS or Android SDK for mobile apps instead.
patches.new_text: The November browser table lists Firefox desktop Apple Pay with the non-Safari desktop `paymentMethods.applePay: 'always'` condition, while Firefox still lacks Link and Klarna. The April table marked Firefox Apple Pay unsupported and its desktop Chromium footnote said macOS-only; November omits that OS restriction without proving support on every desktop OS. In eligible iOS webviews Apple Pay can work; Google Pay can work without a popup, and Android webviews additionally need host Payment Request API support. Link, PayPal, Klarna, and Amazon Pay are marked unsupported in webviews. All browser, currency, setup, and device gates still apply; consider native iOS/Android SDKs for mobile apps.
